sections.history: Thirukkavalampadi is one of the eleven Thirunangur Tirupathis, a cluster of Vishnu temples in and around Thirunangur village in Sirkazhi taluk, about 10 km by road south-south-east of Sirkazhi. Each of the eleven is one of the 108 Divya Desams — the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham — in Chola Nadu, and all were sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Periya Thirumozhi. The presiding lord here is Gopalakrishnan, Krishna, with Rukmini and Satyabhama; sources also name the Thayar as Madavaral Mangai or Sengamala Nachiyar. Its age rests on the Alvar's hymns.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan of the Chola country, with the lord enshrined as Gopalakrishnan beside his consorts Rukmini and Satyabhama. The shrine's identity is bound to its legend of the Parijata, which gives the village its name.
sections.legends: The sthala purana links the name to the Parijata, the flowering tree of Indra's garden. Satyabhama longed for it; Indra refused, and Krishna laid waste the garden — kavalam, from the word for a garden — and brought the Parijata to earth, hence Thirukkavalampadi. Another reading takes kavalam to mean an elephant and padi a grazing ground. The eleven Thirunangur temples share a legend: when Shiva's grief became a wild dance, he multiplied into eleven Rudras, and Vishnu, at his request, appeared in eleven forms, each enshrined in a separate temple.
sections.festivals: The great occasion is the Thirumangai Alvar Mangalasasana Utsavam in the month of Thai (January–February). On or around the day after Thai Amavasai, the eleven festival images come on Garuda vahanas to Thirunangur, to the Manimadam temple, a Garuda Sevai at which seeing all eleven together is held equal to visiting each.
sections.experience: A village shrine set in the paddy country east of Sirkazhi, best visited as part of the Thirunangur circuit of eleven. Pilgrims often time the journey for the Garuda Sevai of Thai, when the eleven lords gather; at other times ask the priests about the Parijata legend and the Alvar's hymns.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkavalampadi is in the Thirunangur group, about 10 km by road south-east of Sirkazhi in Mayiladuthurai district. The nearest railhead is Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai line; the nearest major airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away.
